The current valuation metrics, including a P/B of -5.35x, reflect a disconnect between the company's fundamental efficiency and its market perception [E6].

Furthermore, the stock languishes at the bottom of its valuation range, sitting merely 15% of the way up its 52-week range while offering zero dividend yield to compensate for these severe operational risks [E3, E4]. Furthermore, the negative book value context [E1] does not negate the fundamental earnings acceleration [E39] that distinguishes this business from sector norms.

The bull’s reliance on an ROE of 13.08% [E8] is fundamentally undermined by the company’s negative book value [E1], which renders standard return-on-equity metrics mathematically distorted and economically meaningless. Furthermore, the 3-year compounded profit growth of 1% [E13] demonstrates that the long-term performance is stagnant, failing to keep pace with the sector median profit growth of 15.8% [E42].
